Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 40-year-old postpartum woman with sudden onset (≈1 h) dyspnea at rest, tachycardia, pleuritic-type chest soreness on deep breath, 4 weeks post-C-section, family history of DVT.  
- Most consistent with suspected pulmonary embolism (high likelihood per DDx and clinician concern).  
- Differential also includes acute respiratory infection (medium likelihood) and anxiety/panic (medium likelihood) per DDx; both considered less likely given acute presentation and postoperative VTE risk.  
- Plan: Urgent hospital assessment recommended; patient to self-transport with infant, advised to go promptly. Avoid further codeine until reviewed. Discussed possibility of anticoagulation if PE confirmed.  
- No immediate investigations performed in telehealth setting.  

Management Plan
- Immediate: Patient to attend nearest emergency department today for evaluation of possible pulmonary embolism.  
- Medications: Hold codeine until assessed.  
- Safety net: If symptoms worsen (increased SOB, chest pain, syncope) before arrival, call emergency services (ambulance).  
- Follow-up: Not arranged yet; will depend on hospital findings.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Pulmonary embolism – High likelihood: sudden dyspnea, tachycardia, 4 weeks post-C-section, family history of DVT, pleuritic discomfort.  
2. Acute respiratory infection (viral/bacterial) – Moderate likelihood: new cough; less favored due to abrupt onset and lack of fever.  
3. Anxiety/panic attack (post-partum) – Moderate likelihood: reports stress and palpitations; organic causes prioritized due to VTE risk factors.
